01 / The mark

Recognizable at a glance.

Primary

White and Pastel Lavender on an obsidian circular backing.

Monochrome

One-color white artwork for restrained applications.

Lavender

Single-ink accent version. Use on dark backgrounds.

Ink

Dark artwork for white and light neutral backgrounds.

Clear space and scale

Keep clear space of at least 12% of the mark width on every side. Use the full seal at 64px and above where possible. Small favicon exports are provided and should be checked in their real context.

Technical source

The bust mark is a genuine two-ink path trace of the supplied raster, with no embedded raster. Texture is simplified for scale. The original file remains in the full launch kit.

02 / Color

Pastel Lavender. Quiet foundations.

Pastel Lavender#C3A1F2
Pure White#F4F4F6
Obsidian#0A0A0C
Graphite#1F1F23

Use lavender with purpose

Lavender marks the next action, the result, or the final word. Use broad neutral space, one strong message, and a restrained grid. White is the light-page background; obsidian anchors dark graphics.

Readable combinations

Use obsidian text on Pastel Lavender. On white, use darker lavender ink #7239A8 for small links and text. White body text belongs on obsidian or graphite, not the lavender seed. Primary CTA purple is #8551BF.

Obsidian on lavenderWhite on lavender ink

Strong display. Human reading.

Saira / display

Good work.
Made visible.

Bold 700-800. Tight line-height around 1.05. Sentence case for stories; short uppercase statements for campaign graphics.

Use fewer words before shrinking the type.

Space Grotesk / body and UI

I build cool products, sell great services, and create content that converts.

Regular 400-500 for reading. Semibold 600 for buttons and labels. A clear offer is more useful than a wall of claims.

04 / Voice and visual rules

Show the work. Make the offer clear.

Direct

Name the product, the deliverable, and the next step. Keep the writing specific and easy to scan.

Grounded

Link finished work. Keep waitlist, accounts, prize pools, and personal earnings separate. Paid placements are identified.

Personal

Use first-person founder language. Sound like someone who made the work and can explain what comes next.

Do

  • Keep the mark proportional and give it space.
  • Use grids, pixel blocks, stars, and execution stripes as supporting elements.
  • Use real screenshots and real work photography.

Avoid

  • Do not recolor the mark outside these supplied variants.
  • Do not put small lavender text on white.
  • Do not invent testimonials, client results, or urgency.
  • Do not imply third-party logos endorse this identity.
